candidates.summary: Memdoor, an open-source single-binary coding agent, published a 'team-solve' workflow where five Qwen3.8-27B agents (planner, two ideators, solver, manager, plus a repair worker) solve programming problems by talking only through files on disk; on the first ten LiveCodeBench Hard problems it scored a mean 9.8 of 10 over five passes, versus 9.6 for the original GVS5H harness and 8.0 for Fable 5 in a single call.
facts: Each agent starts from a fresh context and communicates only through files; a script running the sample tests decides success, not a model.
The workflow is eight YAML files with no code and no model named; it rebuilds the method of GVS5H (Lee, 2026) with the authors' prompts, loop and 128K reply cap.
All 50 runs are published with every request, reply, program and grader output; median run took 40 minutes and $0.39, and the 50 runs cost $35.79.

The README states the limits: ten problems not the authors' 100, so 9.8 vs 9.6 is parity not a gain; contamination cannot be ruled out; the Fable 5 column was one call from the authors' files, not run in this harness.
Model ran on OpenRouter; the workflow can point at a local open-weight model.
Hacker News: 259 points (front page, Oct 31).

candidates.summary: Matt Pocock says he is reworking his open-source Sandcastle tool for v1 and floated a pitch: a 'software factory' with six built-in harnesses (Claude Code, Codex and others) or your own, integrations with sandbox providers (Daytona, Vercel, E2B), Inngest/Trigger.dev templates for durable runs, human-in-the-loop over Slack and Discord, and every skill in his repo exposed as an Agent() function such as CodeReview(), ImplementSpec() and Retro().
facts: Posted as a draft pitch asking for feedback ('How does this sound as a pitch'), not a release.
Repliers pushed back that 'software factory' reads like a deck and suggested leading with the Agent()-per-skill idea; others raised default-deny egress for AFK runs and timeouts for Slack approvals.

candidates.summary: Kun Chen reports that after removing code review and CI bottlenecks for his agent fleet, the next limit is GitHub's API rate limit of 5,000 requests per user per hour, which he says is not enough when one user means hundreds of agents working for a human.
facts: Quote: 'TIL github limits 5000 request per user per hour. that's not enough when "a user" means "hundreds of agents working for a human"'.
GitHub's REST API docs set the primary rate limit for authenticated users at 5,000 requests per hour.

candidates.summary: NVIDIA, Breakthrough Listen and the SETI Institute say AI agents at the Allen Telescope Array in Northern California can now steer the instrument, calibrate it, correct incoming data and run models on the live stream from a single natural-language request.
facts: Stack: NVIDIA Holoscan with the DAQIRI library pulls terabits per second of sensor data into GPU memory; CyberEther (SETI Institute) does signal processing on CUDA-X; Nexus, a web-based observatory orchestrator, acts as the agent harness.
The system handles 2.4 terabits per second on RTX PRO 6000 Blackwell GPUs, with inference on premises next to the instrument.
NVIDIA says the pipeline achieved the first real-time AI detection of a pulsar, in the Crab Nebula.
X news summary notes no alien signals are confirmed and scientists check candidates manually.
Surfaced as an X trending story on Nov 1; NVIDIA's post is dated Oct 30.

candidates.summary: Meng To highlighted Epic Games' official 'Unreal Engine Skills for Claude Code' plugin, which lets Claude Code control the Unreal Editor over MCP, calling it his next step into game dev.
facts: The EpicGames GitHub repo README says it exposes hundreds of tools via Unreal's ToolsetRegistry across 30+ toolsets: actors, blueprints, materials, Niagara, Control Rigs, Sequencer, State Trees, widgets, Gameplay Ability System, automation testing.
It ships an unreal-mcp skill and a SessionStart hook that tells Claude to default to Unreal conventions.
The README says it is published in Anthropic's official Claude Code plugin marketplace (claude-plugins-official).
Requires the Unreal Editor running with the ModelContextProtocol and AllToolsets plugins enabled.
GitHub: 1,794 stars; last push Oct 27, 2026 (read this run).
